passages.text: Therefore if you have any encouragement in Christ, if any comfort from His love, if any fellowship with the Spirit, if any affection and compassion, then make my joy complete by being like-minded, having the same love, being united in spirit and purpose.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Philippi.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul urges the believers to live in unity and love.
If you have encouragement from being in Christ, act on it.
If you have comfort from Christ’s love, show it.
If you share in fellowship with the Holy Spirit, remember it.
If you have any affection or compassion, use it.
Make my joy complete.
Be like-minded.
Have the same love for one another.
Be united in spirit.
Be one in purpose.
passages.original: Εἴ τις οὖν παράκλησις ἐν Χριστῷ εἴ τι παραμύθιον ἀγάπης εἴ τις κοινωνία Πνεύματος εἴ τις σπλάγχνα καὶ οἰκτιρμοί πληρώσατέ μου τὴν χαρὰν ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ φρονῆτε τὴν αὐτὴν ἀγάπην ἔχοντες σύμψυχοι τὸ ἓν φρονοῦντες

passages.text: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or empty pride, but in humility consider others more important than yourselves.
passages.sermon:
Do nothing from selfish ambition.
Do nothing from empty pride.
Act with humility.
Consider other people more important than yourself.
passages.original: μηδὲν κατ’ ἐριθείαν μηδὲ κατὰ κενοδοξίαν ἀλλὰ τῇ ταπεινοφροσύνῃ ἀλλήλους ἡγούμενοι ὑπερέχοντας ἑαυτῶν

passages.text: Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christians in Philippi.
He teaches them how to live as followers of Jesus.
Each of you should not focus only on your own interests.
Each of you should also care about the interests of others.
passages.original: μὴ τὰ ἑαυτῶν ἕκαστοι σκοποῦντες ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰ ἑτέρων ἕκαστοι

passages.text: Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, existing in the form of God, did not consider equality with God something to be grasped, but emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in human likeness.
passages.sermon:
Christ Jesus is our example.
He existed in the form of God.
He did not see equality with God as something to hold onto.
He emptied Himself.
He took the form of a servant.
He became like a human being.
Have the same attitude that was in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: Τοῦτο φρονεῖτε ἐν ὑμῖν ὃ καὶ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ Ὃς ἐν μορφῇ Θεοῦ ὑπάρχων οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν ἡγήσατο τὸ εἶναι ἴσα Θεῷ ἀλλὰ ἑαυτὸν ἐκένωσεν μορφὴν δούλου λαβών ἐν ὁμοιώματι ἀνθρώπων γενόμενος

passages.text: And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient to death— even death on a cross.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is God’s Son.
Jesus appeared as a man.
People saw Jesus in human form.
Jesus humbled Himself.
Jesus chose to obey God completely.
Jesus obeyed God even to the point of death.
Jesus died on a cross.
passages.original: καὶ σχήματι εὑρεθεὶς ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἐταπείνωσεν ἑαυτὸν γενόμενος ὑπήκοος μέχρι θανάτου θανάτου δὲ σταυροῦ

passages.text: Therefore God exalted Him to the highest place and gave Him the name above all names, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
passages.sermon:
God exalted Jesus Christ to the highest place.
God gave Jesus the name above every name.
At the name of Jesus, every knee will bow.
Every being in heaven will bow.
Every being on earth will bow.
Every being under the earth will bow.
Every tongue will confess this truth.
Jesus Christ is Lord.
This brings glory to God the Father.
passages.original: Διὸ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς αὐτὸν ὑπερύψωσεν καὶ ἐχαρίσατο αὐτῷ τὸ ὄνομα τὸ ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὄνομα ἵνα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ πᾶν γόνυ κάμψῃ ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ καταχθονίων καὶ πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξομολογήσηται ὅτι ΚΥΡΙΟΣ ΙΗΣΟΥΣ ΧΡΙΣΤΟΣ εἰς δόξαν Θεοῦ Πατρός

passages.text: Therefore, my beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only in my presence, but now even more in my absence, continue to work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Philippi.
He calls them his beloved.
He says they have always obeyed.
They obeyed when Paul was present with them.
He urges them to obey even more when he is absent.
He tells them to continue working out their own salvation.
He tells them to do this with fear and trembling.
passages.original: Ὥστε ἀγαπητοί μου καθὼς πάντοτε ὑπηκούσατε μὴ ὡς ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ μου μόνον ἀλλὰ νῦν πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἐν τῇ ἀπουσίᾳ μου μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου τὴν ἑαυτῶν σωτηρίαν κατεργάζεσθε

passages.text: For it is God who works in you to will and to act on behalf of His good purpose.
passages.sermon:
God works in you.
God gives you the desire to do what is right.
God gives you the power to do what is right.
God does this for His good purpose.
passages.original: Θεὸς γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἐνεργῶν ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ τὸ θέλειν καὶ τὸ ἐνεργεῖν ὑπὲρ τῆς εὐδοκίας

passages.text: Do everything without complaining or arguing, so that you may be blameless and pure, children of God without fault in a crooked and perverse generation, in which you shine as lights in the world as you hold forth the word of life, in order that I may boast on the day of Christ that I did not run or labor in vain.
passages.sermon:
Do everything without complaining.
Do everything without arguing.
This will help you become blameless.
This will help you become pure.
You are children of God.
You must be without fault.
You live among a crooked and perverse generation.
You shine as lights in the world.
You hold out the word of life.
This gives me reason to boast on the day of Christ.
I will know that I did not run in vain.
I will know that I did not labor in vain.
passages.original: Πάντα ποιεῖτε χωρὶς γογγυσμῶν καὶ διαλογισμῶν ἵνα γένησθε ἄμεμπτοι καὶ ἀκέραιοι τέκνα Θεοῦ ἄμωμα μέσον γενεᾶς σκολιᾶς καὶ διεστραμμένης ἐν οἷς φαίνεσθε ὡς φωστῆρες ἐν κόσμῳ λόγον ζωῆς ἐπέχοντες εἰς καύχημα ἐμοὶ εἰς ἡμέραν Χριστοῦ ὅτι οὐκ εἰς κενὸν ἔδραμον οὐδὲ εἰς κενὸν ἐκοπίασα

passages.text: But even if I am being poured out like a drink offering on the sacrifice and service of your faith, I am glad and rejoice with all of you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul serves the church.
Paul speaks to believers who have faith.
Paul says, “Even if I am being poured out like a drink offering.”
Paul means his life is being given for their faith.
Their faith is a sacrifice and service to God.
Paul is glad.
Paul rejoices with all of them.
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ εἰ καὶ σπένδομαι ἐπὶ τῇ θυσίᾳ καὶ λειτουργίᾳ τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν χαίρω καὶ συνχαίρω πᾶσιν ὑμῖν

passages.text: So you too should be glad and rejoice with me.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Philippians.
Paul encouraged the believers.
Paul told them to be glad.
Paul told them to rejoice with him.
passages.original: τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ καὶ ὑμεῖς χαίρετε καὶ συνχαίρετέ μοι

passages.text: Now I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, that I also may be cheered when I learn how you are doing.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Philippians.
Paul trusts in the Lord Jesus.
Paul hopes to send Timothy to the Philippians soon.
Paul wants Timothy to visit them.
Paul wants to hear news about the Philippians.
Paul will be encouraged when he learns how the Philippians are doing.
passages.original: Ἐλπίζω δὲ ἐν Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Τιμόθεον ταχέως πέμψαι ὑμῖν ἵνα κἀγὼ εὐψυχῶ γνοὺς τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν

passages.text: I have nobody else like him who will genuinely care for your needs.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter to the Philippians.
Paul speaks about Timothy.
Paul says, “I have nobody else like Timothy.”
Timothy is unique among Paul’s companions.
Timothy will genuinely care for your needs.
No one else will care for you as Timothy does.
Timothy’s concern for you is sincere.
passages.original: οὐδένα γὰρ ἔχω ἰσόψυχον ὅστις γνησίως τὰ περὶ ὑμῶν μεριμνήσει

passages.text: For all the others look after their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon: All the others seek their own interests.\r\nThey do not seek the interests of Jesus Christ.
passages.original: οἱ πάντες γὰρ τὰ ἑαυτῶν ζητοῦσιν οὐ τὰ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: But you know Timothy’s proven worth, that as a child with his father he has served with me to advance the gospel.
passages.sermon:
Timothy is a faithful servant of Christ.
You know Timothy’s proven character.
He has served with me in the work of the gospel.
He served as a child serves with his father.
He worked with me to advance the message of Jesus.
passages.original: τὴν δὲ δοκιμὴν αὐτοῦ γινώσκετε ὅτι ὡς πατρὶ τέκνον σὺν ἐμοὶ ἐδούλευσεν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον

passages.text: So I hope to send him as soon as I see what happens with me.
passages.sermon: Paul is writing to the Philippians.\r\nPaul hopes to send Timothy to them.\r\nPaul will send Timothy as soon as he knows what will happen to himself.
passages.original: Τοῦτον μὲν οὖν ἐλπίζω πέμψαι ὡς ἂν ἀφίδω τὰ περὶ ἐμὲ ἐξαυτῆς

passages.text: And I trust in the Lord that I myself will come soon.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul trusts in the Lord.
Paul believes he will come soon.
Paul refers to himself.
passages.original: πέποιθα δὲ ἐν Κυρίῳ ὅτι καὶ αὐτὸς ταχέως ἐλεύσομαι

passages.text: But I thought it necessary to send back to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, who is also your messenger and minister to my needs.
passages.sermon:
Epaphroditus is my brother.
He works with me.
He serves as a fellow soldier with me.
He is your messenger.
He ministers to my needs.
I thought it was necessary to send Epaphroditus back to you.
passages.original: Ἀναγκαῖον δὲ ἡγησάμην Ἐπαφρόδιτον τὸν ἀδελφὸν καὶ συνεργὸν καὶ συστρατιώτην μου ὑμῶν δὲ ἀπόστολον καὶ λειτουργὸν τῆς χρείας μου πέμψαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: For he has been longing for all of you and is distressed because you heard he was ill.
passages.sermon:
Epaphroditus is my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier.
He is also your messenger and minister to my needs.
He has been longing for all of you.
He feels distressed.
He knows you heard he was ill.
passages.original: ἐπειδὴ ἐπιποθῶν ἦν πάντας ὑμᾶς καὶ ἀδημονῶν διότι ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἠσθένησεν

passages.text: He was sick indeed, nearly unto death. But God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, to spare me sorrow upon sorrow.
passages.sermon:
Epaphroditus became very sick.
He was almost dead.
God showed mercy to Epaphroditus.
God also showed mercy to me.
God did this so I would not have even more sorrow.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ἠσθένησεν παραπλήσιον θανάτῳ ἀλλὰ ὁ Θεὸς ἠλέησεν αὐτόν οὐκ αὐτὸν δὲ μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐμέ ἵνα μὴ λύπην ἐπὶ λύπην σχῶ

passages.text: Therefore I am all the more eager to send him, so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be less anxious.
passages.sermon:
I am sending him to you very eagerly.
I want you to see him again.
When you see him, you will rejoice.
When you rejoice, I will be less anxious.
passages.original: Σπουδαιοτέρως οὖν ἔπεμψα αὐτὸν ἵνα ἰδόντες αὐτὸν πάλιν χαρῆτε κἀγὼ ἀλυπότερος ὦ

passages.text: Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honor men like him, because he nearly died for the work of Christ, risking his life to make up for your deficit of service to me.
passages.sermon:
Epaphroditus is a servant of Christ.
He worked for Christ.
He almost died while serving Christ.
He risked his life for this work.
He did this to help me.
You could not serve me directly.
He made up for your lack of service to me.
Welcome him in the Lord.
Welcome him with great joy.
Honor people like him.
passages.original: προσδέχεσθε οὖν αὐτὸν ἐν Κυρίῳ μετὰ πάσης χαρᾶς καὶ τοὺς τοιούτους ἐντίμους ἔχετε ὅτι διὰ τὸ ἔργον Χριστοῦ μέχρι θανάτου ἤγγισεν παραβολευσάμενος τῇ ψυχῇ ἵνα ἀναπληρώσῃ τὸ ὑμῶν ὑστέρημα τῆς πρός με λειτουργίας
